label: TMUA 2023 · Paper 1 · Question 10

hints.title: Read the square-root curve geometrically
hints.body: Square the height relation and rearrange it as a circle equation, retaining the sign required by the square root.
hints.recap: A definite integral of a nonnegative curve is its geometric area.
hints.pitfall: The square root selects only part of the circle.
hints.pause: Identify the radius and the exact region under the curve.

recall.reminder: A definite integral of a nonnegative curve is its geometric area.

hints.title: List all strip boundaries
hints.body: Divide the integration interval into four equal strips, then evaluate the height at each boundary.
hints.recap: Four strips require five heights, with only the interior heights doubled.
hints.pitfall: Count strips rather than mistaking the number of heights for the number of strips.
hints.pause: Calculate the trapezium estimate, compare it with the exact area and take the positive difference.

recall.reminder: Four strips require five heights, with only the interior heights doubled.

solution:
1. Recognise the curve. y=4−x2 is the upper half of x2+y2=4, a circle of radius 2. Its integral from −2 to 2 is the semicircle area 2π.

2. Compute the estimate. Four strips have width 1. At x=−2,−1,0,1,2, the heights are 0,3,2,3,0. Thus T=12[0+2(3+2+3)+0]=2+23.

3. Find the positive difference. Chords lie below this semicircle, so the estimate is smaller. The difference is 2π−(2+23)=2(π−1−3). Answer B.
knowledgePattern: Compare a four-strip trapezium estimate with the exact semicircle area
